title: The torsor class is the boundary of one
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $G$ an abelian sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ [def-sc-zariski-site, def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology]. Write $\mathbf Z_X$ for the constant integer sheaf. For every $G$-torsor $T$ [def-sc-gm-torsor] there is a short exact sequence $0\to G\to E\xrightarrow{p}\mathbf Z_X\to0$ of abelian sheaves whose *fibre over $1$*, the sheaf $E\times_{\mathbf Z_X,1}*$ of local lifts of the global section $1$ with $G$ acting by translation, is isomorphic to $T$. The Zariski bijection of [lem-sc-torsor-h1] sends $[T]$ to $\delta_E(1)\in H^1(X_{\mathrm{Zar}},G)$, where $\delta_E:H^0(X_{\mathrm{Zar}},\mathbf Z_X)\to H^1(X_{\mathrm{Zar}},G)$ is the boundary map in the long exact sequence [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology]. Conversely, for every such short exact sequence its fibre over $1$ is a $G$-torsor and its class is $\delta_E(1)$.
